title: 第23章 狱中第24章 撞见
content_zh:
御史台狱坐落在皇城西南角，是一处独立的院落，四周高墙耸立，墙头立着密密麻麻的铁蒺藜，在月光下泛着冷森森的光。
院门外站着两排禁军，甲胄鲜明，手持长戟，目光如鹰隼般扫视着往来之人。
樊义山在门口站定，从袖中取出李利民的手令递了过去。领头的禁军接过，就着灯笼的光仔细核验了一番，又抬头看了樊义山一眼，侧身让开，示意樊义山跨进院门。
樊义山刚跨进院门，立刻有一股阴冷潮湿的气息扑面而来，混着霉味、铁锈味，还有一种说不清道不明的令人作呕的甜腥气。他脚步顿了一下，又继续往里走。
狱卒提着一盏油灯走在前面，灯光昏黄，照得甬道两侧的墙壁隐隐绰绰。水珠从墙壁里渗出来，顺着砖面往下淌。樊义山的靴子踩在湿滑的青砖上，发出沉闷的声响，在狭窄的甬道里来回撞击，像某种不祥的回声。
“杜茂源关在哪里？”他问。
狱卒头也没回：“甲字三号。”
甲字三号在甬道最深处。狱卒在一扇铁门前停下，从腰间摸出一串钥匙，挑了半天，找到其中一把插进锁孔。铁锁发出一声沉闷的咔哒声，锁舌弹开。铁门被推开，发出一声尖利的吱呀声。
“一炷香。”狱卒竖起一根手指，也不等樊义山回答，提着灯走了。
甬道里暗了下来，只剩铁门上方那盏气窗透进来的一点月光，惨白惨白地落在地上，像一滩水渍。
樊义山跨进牢房，杜茂源坐在角落的草堆上，背靠着墙。
身上的青色官袍已经皱得不成样子，膝盖和袖口沾满了草屑和泥灰。他的头发散了大半，原本梳得整整齐齐的发髻歪歪斜斜地挂在脑后，几缕花白的碎发垂在额前，遮住了半边脸。玄铁镣铐锁着他的手脚，粗重的铁链在地上拖出一段距离，一端钉在墙上的铁环里。他的手腕被铁环磨破了皮，暗红色的血痂糊在铁环上，在惨白的月光里泛着黑。
想来在这狱中并没有被善待。
“杜节使。”樊义山开口。
杜茂源的身体微微动了一下，慢慢抬起头，看清了来人，怔了一瞬，继而一喜：“樊女婿。”
“我和令嫒已经退婚了。”樊义山道。
杜茂源脸上的笑容僵了僵。
“那你今夜到访……”
“李相爷让我带句话给你。”樊义山的声音压得很低。
杜茂源的瞳孔微微缩了一下：“李相爷？”

樊义山从袖中取出一张纸条展开，递到杜茂源面前。月光太暗，看不清纸条上的字，但杜茂源没有接，只是看了一眼那张纸条，又抬眼看着樊义山，嘴角微微牵动了一下。
“你念给我听吧。”他道。
樊义山收回纸条，凑到气窗透进来的月光下，将纸条上的内容一字一句念了出来，声音很轻，轻到只有牢房里的两个人能听见，“勾结闽地驻军一事，由你一人承担，不可牵连郑柱。李相爷会保你家中女眷平安，无人受你牵连。你的女儿们嫁娶生计，李相爷都会安排妥当。”
杜茂源听着，脸上的表情瞬息万变。
这件事本就是他一人所为，只不过并不是勾结驻军试图谋反，只不过是害怕郑柱被施舍扳倒后，会殃及自己，而不得已另谋出路，为自己求得一线生机罢了。
只是，这件事竟被施舍那边拿住了把柄，大做文章，把官员的结党营私，上升到谋逆的大罪。
朝堂上的党派纷争而已。
既然如此，他杜茂源也顺水推舟起来。
“让我一人承担？郑柱呢？他当时让我替他联络闽地驻军的时候，不是拍着胸脯说出了事他扛吗？”
樊义山没有回答。这些话不是他该说的，他只是个传话的。
“如果我死了，且是谋逆这等大罪，而被陛下处死，我的女儿们……”他说，“她们真的能平安？你相爷当我杜茂源是个傻子吗？”
樊义山道：“李相爷亲口说的，信与不信，杜节使自有判断。”
杜茂源低下头，看着自己手腕上的玄铁镣铐，看着那些暗红色的血痂。
content_en:
Yushitai Prison is located in the southwest corner of the imperial city. It is an independent courtyard surrounded by high walls. The top of the wall is covered with dense iron caltrops, which glow coldly under the moonlight.
There were two rows of forbidden soldiers standing outside the courtyard gate, wearing bright armor and holding halberds. Their eyes were like hawks scanning the people coming and going.
Fan Yishan stood at the door, took out Li Limin's warrant from his sleeve and handed it over. The leading imperial guard took it, inspected it carefully under the light of the lantern, looked up at Fan Yishan, stepped aside, and signaled Fan Yishan to step into the courtyard gate.
As soon as Fan Yishan stepped into the courtyard gate, he was immediately hit by a cold, damp smell, mixed with the smell of mold, rust, and an indescribable, disgustingly sweet smell. He paused for a moment, then continued walking inside.
The jailer walked in front holding an oil lamp. The light was dim and illuminated the walls on both sides of the corridor. Water droplets seeped out of the wall and trickled down the brick surface. Fan Yishan's boots stepped on the slippery green bricks, making a dull sound, hitting back and forth in the narrow corridor, like some ominous echo.
"Where is Du Maoyuan detained?" he asked.
The jailer didn't even turn around: "Number A, number three."
Number A No. 3 is at the deepest part of the corridor. The jailer stopped in front of an iron door and took out a bunch of keys from his waist. After searching for a long time, he found one and inserted it into the keyhole. The iron lock made a dull click, and the lock tongue popped open. The iron door was pushed open with a sharp creak.
"A stick of incense." The jailer raised a finger and left without waiting for Fan Yishan's answer.
The corridor became dark, and only a little bit of moonlight filtered through the transom above the iron door, falling pale and pale to the ground, like a puddle of water stains.
Fan Yishan stepped into the cell, and Du Maoyuan was sitting on the haystack in the corner, leaning against the wall.
The green official robe on his body was wrinkled and his knees and cuffs were stained with grass clippings and mud. Most of his hair was loose, and the neatly combed bun hung crookedly on the back of his head. A few strands of gray hair hung in front of his forehead, covering half of his face. Dark iron shackles locked his hands and feet. The thick iron chain was dragged a distance on the ground, and one end was nailed into the iron ring on the wall. His wrist was scratched by the iron ring, and dark red blood scabs were stuck on the iron ring, glowing black in the pale moonlight.
I guess I was not treated well in this prison.
"Envoy Du Jie." Fan Yishan said.
Du Maoyuan's body moved slightly, and he slowly raised his head and saw the person clearly. He was startled for a moment, and then he said happily: "Son-in-law Fan."
"My daughter and I have broken off our engagement." Fan Yishan said.
The smile on Du Maoyuan's face froze.
"Then you're here tonight..."
"Prime Minister Li asked me to bring you a message." Fan Yishan's voice was very low.
Du Maoyuan's pupils shrank slightly: "Master Li?"
Fan Yishan took out a piece of paper from his sleeve, unfolded it, and handed it to Du Maoyuan. The moonlight was too dark to see clearly the words on the note, but Du Maoyuan didn't answer it. He just glanced at the note, then looked up at Fan Yishan, the corners of his mouth twitching slightly.
"Read it to me," he said.
Fan Yishan took back the note, leaned under the moonlight that filtered through the transom, and read out the contents of the note word for word. His voice was very soft, so soft that only the two people in the cell could hear, "You alone are responsible for colluding with the Fujian garrison, and Zheng Zhu cannot be implicated. Mr. Li will keep the female family members of your family safe, and no one will be implicated by you. Mr. Li will make arrangements for your daughters to marry and earn a living."
Du Maoyuan listened, the expression on his face changed rapidly.
This incident was his own doing, but he did not collude with the garrison to attempt rebellion. He was just afraid that Zheng Zhu would be brought down by alms, which would bring disaster to him, so he had no choice but to find another way out to get a chance for himself.
However, the charity side actually took advantage of this matter and made a big fuss, elevating officials' clique for personal gain to a serious crime of rebellion.
Party strife in the courtThat’s all.
In this case, Du Maoyuan also followed suit.
"Let me bear the responsibility alone? Where is Zheng Zhu? When he asked me to contact the Fujian garrison for him, didn't he pat his chest and say that he would take the responsibility if anything happened?"
Fan Yishan did not answer. These words are not what he should say, he is just a messenger.
"If I die and am executed by Your Majesty for such a serious crime as treason, my daughters..." he said, "will they really be safe? Do you, Prime Minister, think that I, Du Maoyuan, am a fool?"
Fan Yishan said: "Mr. Li said it himself. Whether you believe it or not, Du Jie will make his own judgment."
Du Maoyuan lowered his head and looked at the dark iron shackles on his wrists and the dark red blood scabs.
